# A non-ok status is not permission to leave it broken: it is a claim that
# somebody looked. Refresh with `sh tools/golden_compile.sh --update` and
# review the diff -- a new failure means the generator started emitting C that
# does not build or does not load.
# measured on aarch64 with clang 19 at -mcpu=v1

column3: recursion: fib calls itself, and the verifier refuses BPF-to-BPF recursion ("recursive call from fib_inner() to fib_inner()"). Inherent to eBPF, not kernel-specific. The verdict on this one is that it fails at the wrong LAYER -- a partition or validation check could name it -- rather than that it is a wrong program. Detecting it statically is a named follow-up, not done here.

signed division (`@b * @h / 2`): the BPF ISA has no signed division before v4, and the CLI pins -mcpu=v1. Measured to be fine at -mcpu=v4. This is legal Ruby; the workaround in the DSL is divu. A real ISA constraint, loud, but diagnosed by clang rather than by us.

negative fixture: kfield_str_eq written without its compare literal, so the field path silently loses its last hop and ends on `struct dentry *`. The static shape check refuses it and names this Ruby call. If this ever turns `ok`, that check has been weakened and reading a struct pointer as a string is back.

the kernel kfunc filter, not us: bpf_qdisc_init_prologue is refused with -EACCES. Measured: hand-written C calling it DIRECTLY from the SEC("struct_ops/init") entry is refused identically, bpf_qdisc_reset_destroy_epilogue is refused the same way, and the same qdisc with both kfuncs dropped loads fine. May differ on another kernel.
